option_relations.rationale: Leptomeningeal lymphoma, especially with B-cell origin and plasmacytic differentiation, can manifest as neurolymphomatosis when it infiltrates the peripheral nervous system or cranial nerves, as suggested by the vagus nerve enhancement.
Leptomeningeal lymphoplasmacytic lymphoma (LPL) is a type of lymphoma that can involve the central and peripheral nervous system, leading to neurolymphomatosis.

Waldenström macroglobulinemia (WM) is a lymphoplasmacytic lymphoma that can involve the CNS (Bing-Neel syndrome), and this CNS infiltration can present as neurolymphomatosis if it affects cranial or peripheral nerves.
Leptomeningeal involvement by relapsed B-cell lymphoma (lymphomatous meningitis) can cause neurolymphomatosis if the lymphoma cells infiltrate the cranial or peripheral nerves.
